assertions.text: Package options (fragile, insuredValue, handling) are collapsed into a single map column like [fragile: true, insuredValue: 500] — not kept as three separate columns
assertions.evidence: Table has three separate columns: | Fragile | Insured Value | Handling |, not a single Options map column

assertions.text: A @TypeConverter method is present that accepts Map<String, String> (or similar) and returns PackageOptions
assertions.evidence: No @TypeConverter method present; options constructed manually in test body with if statements

assertions.text: Dimensions are represented as a [L, W, H] list in the table — not as three separate columns

assertions.evidence: Same rate all carriers | ... | {DHL, UPS, FEDEX} | 12.00

assertions.text: Multiple @TableTest methods exist, each addressing a distinct concern — not one monolithic table

assertions.text: Weight and cost parameters use BigDecimal (not double or String). Dimensions use Integer or int.
assertions.evidence: void calculateShippingCost(..., BigDecimal weight, List<Integer> dimensions, ..., BigDecimal expected)

assertions.text: Each table has a scenario/description column as the leftmost column
assertions.evidence: Scenario | Region | Service | ... (Scenario is leftmost column)

assertions.text: Scenario names describe conditions — not outcomes or generic labels
assertions.evidence: EU standard light, Fragile surcharge, Dimensional weight override, Hazmat handling, Oversize surcharge

assertions.text: At least one output column name ends with '?' (e.g. 'Cost?', 'Base rate?')
Column names use domain language — not code identifiers
assertions.evidence: Region, Service, Weight, Dimensions, Fragile, Insured Value, Handling, Carrier, Cost? (plain English, not camelCase)

assertions.text: Test method bodies contain no if or switch statements
Annotations appear in order: @DisplayName (if present), @Description (if present), @TableTest
assertions.evidence: @TableTest annotation present with no prior @DisplayName or @Description

assertions.text: Each test method has a @DisplayName annotation or a method name that reads as a clear descriptive title
